jp: 新幹線[しんかんせん]{は|wa-topic}速[はや]いです。飛行機[ひこうき]{も|mo-also}速[はや]いです。
en: The Shinkansen is fast. Planes are fast too.
why: Adding a second thing with the same property ('too') is も; は would set planes apart.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-contrast}便利[べんり]です。でも、バス{は|wa-contrast}不便[ふべん]です。
en: The train is convenient. But the bus is inconvenient.
why: Convenient and inconvenient are opposites, so the bus is contrasted with は; も would say it is convenient too.

jp: この電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}昼[ひる]{は|wa-contrast}空[す]いています。でも、朝[あさ]{は|wa-contrast}とても混[こ]んでいます。
en: This train is empty at midday. But in the morning it is very crowded.
why: Empty and crowded are opposites, so morning is contrasted with は; も would mean it is empty in the morning too.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}地下鉄[ちかてつ]{で|de-means}行[い]きます。妹[いもうと]{も|mo-also}地下鉄[ちかてつ]{で|de-means}行[い]きます。
en: I go by subway. My younger sister goes by subway too.
why: Your sister does the same thing, so も adds her; は would contrast her with you.

jp: 先週[せんしゅう]、京都[きょうと]{に|ni-destination}行[い]きました。大阪[おおさか]{に|ni-destination}{も|mo-also}行[い]きました。
en: Last week I went to Kyoto. I went to Osaka too.
why: Osaka is a second place on the same trip, so も ('too') is right; には would contrast it with Kyoto.

jp: この町[まち]{に|ni-location}{は|wa-contrast}駅[えき]{が|ga-existence}あります。でも、空港[くうこう]{は|wa-contrast}ありません。
en: This town has a station. But there is no airport.
why: Station and airport are set against each other, so は contrasts them; も would mean no airport either.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]{も|mo-both}地図[ちず]{も|mo-both}忘[わす]れました。
en: I forgot both the ticket and the map.
why: A 'both A and B' pair needs も after each noun; 切符は would set the ticket apart instead of pairing it.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{は|wa-contrast}遠[とお]いです{が|ga-but}、駅[えき]{は|wa-contrast}近[ちか]いです。
en: The airport is far, but the station is near.
why: Far and near are opposites, so the station is contrasted with は; も would say it is far too.
